I don't believe that any life boats launched completely filled and the ship was only equipped with enough to save something like half of the passengers. A lot of boats that night launched when they were half full or less than half full. First class passengers were extremely reluctant to get on, and men and maybe some third class passengers were barred from getting on the lifeboats initially. What you said is totally wrong. Oh, by the way, if you don't make it on to a boat and end up in the water, you would have an extremely low chance of surviving. The water was probably 40-45 degrees Fahrenheit and you would freeze very very quickly.

To save the maximum, send a group to immediately radio SoS signals, another to gather signal flares and start firing in regular intervals, have another group start making rafts from buoyant furniture.

Load up the lifeboats to the maximum capacity and lower them early on. No able bodied man or woman can get a seat without working for a time on a work detail. This takes care of almost half the people on the ship.

Construct the rafts on the deck and have handholds set up for passengers to hold firm once the ship goes under. The rafts will surface and it's important to stay with them.

Get everyone in a life jacket and distribute the life preservers in groups.

Unlock the lower decks so that all passengers can help make rafts. Arm the crew and have the crew lead work details for all these tasks; if everyone is busy there will be less panic. Keep the music playing and have organized breaks for food and drink. Bust out any and all supplies. Have ministers that will counsel and calm passengers through prayer or in conversation, but do so mainly while working.

We have 3 hours people, let's get to it! Every life can be saved!
Good plan. I can see that you've been on the Titanic before.
Look for anything that floats and hope people wont freeze to death before help arrives.

Find shit that floats, build shit that floats, make shit float. There is one fundamental threat to survival - you're in the mutherfucking North Atlantic and the water is so cold people die after 6-8 mins in the water. The water might as well be lava.

Round up work parties to gather anything that they can find that floats. Furniture, crates, barrels, tires and cordage, sheets and canvas to hold it together. Set others to work lashing it together into rafts. Aim for 15 person to a raft, but make whatever you can get that will hold together.

Get everybody you can into heavy wool, blankets etc. If you have to swim for more than a minute, you're pretty much dead anyways. Wet wool will trap enough body heat to keep you alive.
